edits.new: Borage (Borago officinalis), also called starflower, is a large, fast-growing, frost-tender annual herb in the borage family (Boraginaceae), native to the Mediterranean. It builds a bushy, sprawling plant about 2 to 3 ft tall and 12 to 16 in wide, clothed in coarse, bristly, gray-green leaves, and carries loose clusters of nodding, star-shaped, sky-blue flowers from late spring into fall. Borage is one of the best bee and pollinator plants a garden can grow, a traditional companion set near tomatoes, squash, and strawberries, and a vigorous self-seeder that naturalizes readily once established. Both the cucumber-flavored young leaves and the blue flowers are edible, used fresh as a garnish and in drinks and salads, though borage is best eaten in moderation. It grows through the warm months in cool and temperate regions and is killed by hard frost; in hot, humid climates it is grown instead as a cool-season plant.
